descriptionChirho: Moral or ritual impurity, filthiness, or corruption, used in the NT primarily for sexual immorality and moral defilement (Rom 1:24, 6:19; 2 Cor 12:21; Gal 5:19; Eph 4:19, 5:3; Col 3:5; 1 Thess 2:3, 4:7). All 10 occurrences across accusative, dative, nominative, and genitive singular cases convey the same abstract moral concept. Multilingual translations are fully consistent: Spanish 'impureza,' Arabic 'najasa' (نجاسة), Hindi 'ashuddhataa' (अशुद्धता), Korean 'deoreoum/bujeonham' (더러움/부정함), Swahili 'uchafu.' The two clusters differ only in case inflection, not in semantic content.
